title: Split Kakeya sets over F_3 and explicit Kakeya sets below Lev's 2009 pattern in every dimension n >= 6
made_with: AI agents working in MV2's name (MV2, Munim, Inc.); not checked by a human mathematician
definitions: K in F_3^m is a Kakeya set if it contains a full line {a, a+d, a+2d} in every direction d. A split of K is a pair (A, B) with A u B = K and C(A, B) = {b - a : a in A, b in B, -(a + b) in K} = F_3^m; its excess is e = |A n B| >= 1. See k9/SPLIT.md.

lemmas.lemma_1: If (A, B) is a split of K with excess e, then {0} x K u {1} x A u {2} x B is a Kakeya set of F_3^(m+1) with 2|K| + e points, and it has a split with excess e again (Corollary).
lemmas.lemma_2: If K' is any Kakeya set of F_3^(m+1) whose layer x0 = 0 is K, a split of K lifts to a split of K' with the same excess.
lemmas.status: proved by hand in k9/SPLIT.md; not checked by a human mathematician; every instance used below is also verified by computer

family.formula: 845 * 2^(n-9) - 1 points in F_3^n for every n >= 9
family.note: Lemma 1 applied n - 9 times to the 844-point set with its excess-1 split. Size / 2^n tends to 845/512 = 1.6504, against 5/3 = 1.6667 for Lev's pattern and 2 for the classical construction. The gap to the pattern is 25 * 2^n / 1536 + 1 + (-1)^n / 3 points, which grows without bound.

limits: Upper bounds only; nothing here says any of these sizes is optimal. For large n the random construction of Kopparty, Lev, Saraf and Sudan (arXiv:1003.3736) has growth base about 1.8899 < 2, so it is far smaller than any c * 2^n family; this family is about explicit sets in moderate dimension.
